name: China Mobile Limited
executive_summary: China Mobile is the dominant mainland Chinese mobile operator, screening as a buy on cheapness (P/E 11.2, P/B 1.1), a 6.2% dividend yield, and low leverage (debt/equity ~7%), with 13 of 22 quantitative models passing across all four value families. The investment case rests on a quasi-monopoly franchise generating over CNY 1tn of annual revenue, rising shareholder returns (dividend raised to CN¥2.75 per share in 2025), and a valuation that prices in minimal growth despite steady top-line expansion. The central debate is whether 2025’s sharp free-cash-flow contraction and persistent heavy capex—together with state-linked governance and regulatory oversight—justify a deep discount, or whether they structurally cap total returns. Primary HKEX/annual-report filing bodies were not retrieved in this research pack; financial trends below rely on Yahoo Finance aggregates and should be treated as indicative pending verification against published results.
investment_thesis: The quantitative screen flags China Mobile as a classic value-and-income compounder rather than a deep cyclical or distressed name. It passes Graham Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Earnings Quality—covering cheapness, dividend, GARP, and risk families with full metric coverage (20/20) and sector-relative composite of 64%. Business quality supports the screen: revenue has grown from CNY 937bn (2022) to CNY 1,050bn (2025) per Yahoo data, net income has risen from CNY 125bn to a plateau near CNY 137–138bn, and the balance sheet is conservatively geared with total debt of CNY 101bn against common equity of CNY 1,429bn (2025). Operating cash flow has remained robust (CNY 233–316bn annually, 2022–2025), funding both a rising dividend (CNY 87bn → CNY 103bn cash dividends paid) and substantial network investment. For a value investor, the hook is a high-quality incumbent trading below book-adjusted intrinsic estimates implied by double-digit earnings yield and a yield above fixed-income alternatives, with limited balance-sheet risk. The screen’s failures—Graham Defensive, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Piotroski F-Score (4/9), Financial Health—signal that this is not a “quality compounder at any price” story; conviction should rest on valuation and cash return, not on accelerating ROIC or margin expansion.
financial_review:
**Source limitation:** The filings index (`filings_index.json`) contains zero entries—no annual reports, interim results, trading updates, or SEC 20-F/6-K bodies under `filings/bodies/`. All figures below are sourced from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance); no primary filing extracts were available for cross-check. Interim/H1 2025 or Q1 2026 disclosure language (going concern, contingencies, covenants) could not be reviewed.

**Revenue and profitability (Yahoo, CNY):**
| Period | Revenue | Operating income | Net income | Diluted EPS |
|--------|---------|------------------|------------|-------------|
| 2022 | 937.3bn | 135.0bn | 125.5bn | 5.88 |
| 2023 | 1,009.3bn | 144.4bn | 131.8bn | 6.15 |
| 2024 | 1,040.8bn | 158.0bn | 138.4bn | 6.42 |
| 2025 | 1,050.2bn | 157.8bn | 137.1bn | n/a (Q1 EPS 1.42 only) |

Revenue growth has been steady but decelerating (+1% y/y in 2025). Operating income peaked in 2024 and was flat-to-down in 2025; net income dipped ~1% to CNY 137.1bn. Normalised earnings trends are obscured by recurring special charges/write-offs (CNY 8.9–15.4bn range, 2022–2025).

**Cash flow and capital allocation (Yahoo, CNY):**
| Period | Operating CF | CapEx | Free cash flow | Dividends paid |
|--------|-------------|-------|----------------|----------------|
| 2022 | 280.8bn | (189.6bn) | 91.2bn | 86.8bn |
| 2023 | 303.8bn | (181.3bn) | 122.5bn | 91.1bn |
| 2024 | 315.7bn | (156.0bn) | 159.8bn | 97.5bn |
| 2025 | 232.9bn | (157.0bn) | 76.0bn | 103.4bn |

2025 marks a material inflection: operating cash flow fell ~26% y/y and FCF nearly halved versus 2024, driven in part by a CNY 70bn working-capital outflow (receivables and payables shifts). Capex remains elevated at ~CNY 157bn (~15% of revenue), consistent with 5G rollout and digital infrastructure spend. Dividends continued to rise despite the FCF squeeze, implying payout supported by balance-sheet liquidity rather than incremental free cash in 2025.

**Balance sheet (Yahoo, CNY, year-end 2025):** Total assets CNY 2,128bn; stockholders’ equity CNY 1,428bn; total debt CNY 101bn (predominantly capital-lease obligations, CNY 91bn); cash and equivalents CNY 97bn (down from CNY 167bn at end-2024); short-term investments CNY 211bn. Working capital is negative (CNY −116bn). Non-current pension and post-retirement obligations are modest at CNY 6.6bn. Goodwill and intangibles total CNY 103bn; tangible book value CNY 1,326bn. Net debt is effectively nil given cash plus liquid investments.

**Gaps:** No audited annual or interim filing text to confirm revenue recognition policies, related-party transactions, regulatory fee structures, or segment breakdown (personal, home, business, emerging markets). Quarterly income data in the pack covers only Q1 2025 (EPS 1.42). Full-year 2025 EPS and any 2026 interim results are absent from primary sources.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and policy:** As a state-influenced telecom incumbent, China Mobile faces tariff guidance, “common prosperity” dividend expectations, data-security rules, and potential forced infrastructure sharing—all of which can cap pricing power and ROE (~9.6% per screen) without appearing on the balance sheet. Filing language on these risks was unavailable in this pack.

**Capex and FCF sustainability:** Heavy, persistent capex (CNY 155–190bn annually, 2022–2025) and the 2025 FCF collapse raise questions about whether reported earnings translate reliably into distributable cash. The screen’s failure on Financial Health and a Piotroski score of 4/9 (ROA, leverage, current ratio, gross margin, and asset turnover all deteriorating or flat) align with this concern.

**Working capital and receivables:** Accounts receivable grew to CNY 99.8bn gross (allowance CNY 41.5bn) in 2025; the CNY 31.7bn receivables increase contributed to negative operating cash conversion in 2025. Without filing detail, it is unclear how much reflects government/enterprise payment cycles versus collection stress.

**Governance:** Board turnover in 2026 (resignation of executive director Wang Limin, 24 Jun 2026; updated committee line-up, 16 Jun 2026) is noted in news but not corroborated in filing bodies. State ownership limits minority influence on capital allocation and M&A.

**Competition:** China Telecom and China Unicom remain rational competitors; broader risk lies in OTT substitution and cloud/AI capex arms race requiring continued spend without commensurate ARPU gains.

**Missing filing disclosures:** Going-concern statements, litigation contingencies, covenant terms, and pension assumptions could not be assessed—an explicit verify-before-trade gap.
news_highlights:
Company-specific coverage over the past year is thin and partly noisy; several manifest hits are unrelated (Taiwan market flow, Deutsche Telekom/T-Mobile M&A, academic papers). Material items:

- **“China Mobile (HKG:941) Has Announced That It Will Be Increasing Its Dividend To CN¥2.75”** (Simply Wall St, 12 Aug 2025) — supports the dividend-growth pillar of the screen.
- **“China Mobile (SEHK:941): A Closer Look at Valuation After Steady Share Price Gains This Year”** (Yahoo Finance, 2 Oct 2025) — notes ~12% YTD share-price gain and steady fundamentals.
- **“Some Shareholders Feeling Restless Over China Mobile Limited's (HKG:941) P/E Ratio”** (Simply Wall St, 11 Nov 2025) — market debate on whether low P/E reflects opportunity or structural ceiling.
- **“China Mobile Limited (HKG:941) First-Quarter Results: Here's What Analysts Are Forecasting For This Year”** (Simply Wall St, 23 Apr 2026) — Q1 results context; no hard numbers in manifest summary.
- **“China Mobile Limited Announces Resignation of Wang Limin from Executive Director, Effective June 24, 2026”** (MarketScreener, 24 Jun 2026) — governance change.
- **“China Mobile Sets Out Updated Board and Committee Line-Up”** (TipRanks, 16 Jun 2026) — board restructuring.

No manifest entries flagged major M&A, regulatory fines, or strategy pivots in the past year. **News coverage is thin** for operational detail; strategy shifts (cloud, AI, international) are not well documented in this feed.
research_rationale: Quantitative cheapness, dividend yield, and balance-sheet strength support the screen’s buy signal, but absent primary filings and with 2025 FCF deterioration unverified at source, deep research confirms the income/value angle while leaving quality and cash-conversion durability unresolved.
